## Task statement

**Invariant.** Any externally-sourced value is shape/type/range/path-validated before use; failures surface as `MalformedInput`

**Oracle.** structural Hypothesis fuzz → only declared exceptions; a `MalformedInput` reaches the framework's single handler

**Violation cases seeded.** unvalidated dict/list/option node; non-finite float; absolute/`..` path

Source: `EVALS-PLAN.md` Layer 0.

## Construction

Every task is a directory `evals/cases/P1/<case>/` holding a `case.yaml` (the task record: `id`, `property`, `origin`, `grader`, `expect`, `description`, `canary`), a `vuln/` tree with exactly one planted violation, and a `clean/` twin — the same code with the violation fixed through the toolkit primitive. The grader scores both: the violation must be detected in `vuln/` (recall) and not in `clean/` (precision), so the clean twin is the baseline scored alongside every task.

Origins, in the priority order of EVALS-PLAN.md Layer 2:

- **historical-miss** (3): a real miss from this program, encoded permanently.
- **derived** (2): a violation case from the Layer 0 row, in a code shape the historical cases do not already cover.

| task | origin | grader | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `P1-dict-field-string-01` | derived | `fuzz` | A dict-typed field ("controls", a name -> config map) receives a string, list or number; the envelope was checked but the field was assumed, so .items() raises an undeclared AttributeError. Clean passes the field through as_dict. |
| `P1-list-element-method-01` | derived | `fuzz` | A request handler method validates the JSON body and its "fields" list but not each element, so a str/int/None/list element raises an undeclared AttributeError (HTTP 500). Clean routes every element through as_dict/as_str, so the only failure is MalformedInput. |
| `P1-nonfinite-float-01` | historical-miss | `refuse` | smart-dispatch forecast API: ?marginal_cost= went from request.args through float(), which accepts "nan", "inf" and "1e999"; the NaN propagated into the margin and the response serialised as invalid JSON. Clean routes the parameter through secprim.finite_float with a range, so a non-finite value is a MalformedInput (HTTP 422) at the boundary. |
| `P1-option-node-shape-01` | historical-miss | `fuzz` | firstplay parse_ashby_dom: the control list was validated but each option node was not, so {"options": ["a"]} raised an undeclared AttributeError (HTTP 500). Clean routes every node through the shared validators. |
| `P1-path-from-content-01` | historical-miss | `refuse` | study-hub Ledger: every write resolved `self.root / relpath`, where relpath came straight from upstream (a Canvas filename, a Piazza resource name, a page slug). Path replaces the base when the right-hand side is absolute and `..` walks upward, so a hostile name landed outside courses/<slug>/. Clean resolves every destination through secprim.contained_path. |

## Metrics and current numbers

- **recall** = tasks whose `vuln/` the grader detected ÷ tasks, Wilson 95% CI.
- **precision** = tasks whose `clean/` the grader did not flag ÷ tasks, Wilson 95% CI.
- with `--trials K > 1`: **pass@k** (any of k) and **pass^k** (all of k) over tasks.

## Known limitations

From the grader docstrings (what each oracle can and cannot decide):

### `fuzz`

> P1: the safe-degradation property. Detected = an undeclared exception.
>
> Deterministic by construction: `expect.examples` (the known trigger shapes) are
> tried first, then Hypothesis runs derandomized so a run is reproducible. Recall
> on a case therefore never depends on the random seed.

### `refuse`

> Plugin grader `refuse` — the refusal oracle for P1 (boundary) and P2 (bounded
> cost). `fuzz` detects an *undeclared* exception and `cost` detects *time*; neither
> expresses "this input must be turned away": a `float()` that accepts "nan", a
> `root / relpath` that accepts "../x", a reader with no byte cap, an XML parser
> that accepts an entity declaration. Those all *return normally*. This grader
> feeds a fixed, hostile input set and requires a declared refusal for each.
>
>   refuse   expect: {target: "mod:fn",
>                     inputs: <named set> | [<value> | {kind: ..., ...}, ...],
>                     accept: <named set> | [...],        # optional: must NOT be refused
>                     refuse: [TooLarge],                 # exception names that count as a refusal
>                     max_read: N}                        # optional: bytes a target may consume first
>
> Named sets (literal values):
>   nonfinite    nan / inf in every spelling a query parameter can carry
>   finite_ok    ordinary numbers and numeric strings
>   path_escape  absolute, `..`, drive, UNC, NUL, empty — what contained_path refuses
>   path_ok      ordinary relative paths that stay inside the root
>
> Constructed inputs ({kind: ..., size: N, ...}):
>   zip_member   the PATH of a zip archive whose one member (`member`, default
>                "data.bin") declares `size` bytes of `fill` (compressible, the
>                default, or random); decompressed bytes are counted
>   response     a fake HTTP response of `size` bytes with .read/.iter_bytes/
>                .iter_content/.content/.text; bytes handed out are counted
>   xml_dtd      bytes of an XML document carrying an internal entity declaration
>
> A variant is DETECTED when any hostile input is not refused — the target returns,
> raises something outside `refuse`, or (counted kinds) consumes more than
> `max_read` bytes before refusing. An `accept` input that *is* refused is an
> error, not a pass: a twin that refuses everything proves nothing.
>
> Deterministic and offline: inputs are built in memory or in a temp dir, nothing
> depends on the clock, and the stdlib `zipfile` patch used for counting is
> restored in a `finally`.

## Contamination policy

- **Canary.** Every `case.yaml`, every registry entry and `tasks.jsonl` carry the string in `evals/registry/CANARY.txt` (BIG-bench convention): a model that can reproduce it has seen this corpus in training, and its scores on it do not measure the property.
- **Split.** This eval is `split: build`. Build-split cases are used to tune rules and defenses. The held-out split (`evals/heldout/`, EVALS-PLAN.md Phase 4) is sealed: written after the defenses, never used for tuning, and scored only in reports.
- **No model in the loop.** Every grader is deterministic code; no LLM judges a result, so there is nothing to contaminate on the grading side.
